clue.text: Get at a can on the outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the can sits on the outside, wrapped round the single letter that follows 'a'

parts.note: a can is a tin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to reach a can by going round its outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' looks like a description of the can; it tells you the can goes round the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to reach or achieve it, a synonym of getting it.

clue.text: Evil turn makes malignant

indicators.note: the two words are worked into something new, so their letters are rearranged to form the result

explanation.surface: A wicked change of heart turns someone malevolent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' signals the rearrangement of all eight letters of EVIL TURN; 'turn' looks like the indicator but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A virulent disease or attitude is harmful and spiteful, the same sense as malignant.

clue.text: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?

definitions.text: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?

parts.words: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?
parts.note: read as halting a car en route, said as the phrase for stopping the car so that someone may go to Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy

explanation.surface: A traveller breaks a journey to catch an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A pull-up is a stop or roadside halt; Carmen is Bizet's opera, so the phrase is read literally as a stop for that opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling up is stopping a vehicle, and Carmen is the best-known Bizet opera.

clue.text: Type of ground to soak up the moisture

definitions.text: Type of ground to soak up the moisture

parts.words: Type of ground to soak up the moisture
parts.note: a stretch of land described as absorbing wet weather, with the word for rain sitting at the end of the word for land

explanation.surface: Gardening advice about soil that drinks in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The land word ends in RAIN, the moisture it soaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a tract of land considered for its physical features, a type of ground.

clue.text: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on

definitions.text: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on

parts.words: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on
parts.note: describes a caller who turns up unannounced at the door

explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected caller is one nobody planned to see arrive.

clue.text: A press organisation that's thin on the ground

indicators.note: organising the words means putting their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper group whose staff are few and far between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges the six letters of A PRESS; it looks like part of 'press organisation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scanty or scattered, exactly what thin on the ground says.

clue.text: Not bound to deliver

definitions.meaning: to release or liberate someone, as from captivity

explanation.definitionFit: Unrestricted describes the adjective, and to release someone is the verb sense, so both readings fit.

clue.text: The case for a sewer?

parts.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, not a drain, and the case holds needles

explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' suggests a drain; it is a person who sews, and the answer is a needle case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and other sewing items.

clue.text: A custom put to some purpose

definitions.meaning: a habit or usual practice, as in 'usage'
to employ something for a task

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means an established practice; as a verb, to employ or apply something.

clue.text: High court judge at Wimbledon

parts.note: not a legal official but the tennis official seated in a tall chair beside the court

explanation.walkthrough: 'High court judge' suggests the law; Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, where the official sits high above the court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the chair official who rules on play is the umpire.

clue.text: Physical training instructor?

definitions.meaning: done with the hands, as in physical labour
a handbook that teaches how to do something

explanation.surface: A gym coach is introduced to new recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual labour is physical work, and a manual is a book of instructions.

clue.text: Witty cross-talk

parts.note: quick clever exchanges back and forth in conversation

explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty reply and banter between speakers.

clue.text: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?

definitions.text: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?

parts.words: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?
parts.note: a person lacking the benefits that come from being born into wealth or rank

explanation.definitionFit: The underprivileged lack the social and economic advantages others enjoy.

clue.text: Obsolete European currency unit

parts.note: a pre-euro accounting unit of the European Community, whose name is formed from the initials of its full title

explanation.definitionFit: The ecu was a basket currency used in Europe before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Some haven to which no-one returns

parts.note: a port is a haven for ships

indicators.note: returning means the letters for no-one are read backwards

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A harbour from which nobody ever comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' splits as 'no' plus 'one', the Roman numeral I; 'returns' turns that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a part or share, which is what 'some' means as a noun.

clue.text: Have to make some acknowledgment

explanation.definitionFit: It means to possess something, and also to confess or concede a fact.

clue.text: A detour wrongly announced

indicators.note: taking the wrong route suggests the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the letters of A DETOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To read out a statement is to announce it aloud to listeners.

clue.text: The extent to which diets can vary

indicators.note: letting the words vary means their letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A remark on how widely eating plans can differ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vary' rearranges the letters of DIETS and CAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the amount of space between points, an extent.

clue.text: Widespread information leading to real trouble

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of the next one

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: troubling the word disturbs its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Public knowledge that sparks genuine difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British slang for information; 'trouble' rearranges the letters of 'real' and 'leading to' puts the slang word first.
explanation.definitionFit: General means affecting most people or places, so widespread.

clue.text: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?

definitions.text: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?

parts.words: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?
parts.note: in double-entry bookkeeping receipts go in the right-hand column of the ledger, so 'rightly' means on the right side

explanation.walkthrough: 'rightly' seems to mean correctly; it means on the right, where credits sit in an accounts ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means favourable or in credit, and credits are entered on the right of a ledger.

clue.text: A messenger detained outside Burlington House

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, placing it outside

parts.note: held means detained
the Royal Academy (RA) is housed at Burlington House in London

explanation.surface: A courier is held up outside a London building.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly in London is home to the Royal Academy of Arts; 'outside' means the word for detained wraps round its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald is an official who carries messages and proclamations.

clue.text: Move at twice the speed?

parts.note: the military order to run at a quickened pace, read as going at twice the speed

explanation.definitionFit: To go at the double is to run or hurry, as soldiers do on command.

clue.text: Variety of 12 that should ultimately bear fruit

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the 12 answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a word for witty banter

explanation.surface: A new form of banter that will pay off in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges the letters of REPARTEE, the answer at 12.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit tree of this kind will in time produce its crop, so it should bear fruit.

clue.text: Simple kind of chair

explanation.definitionFit: It means not hard, and an easy chair is a large comfortable armchair.

clue.text: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition

definitions.text: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition

parts.words: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition
parts.note: the boy of Greek myth who flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means belonging to fable, not wonderful; 'soaring' is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son flew too high, the wax melted, and he fell into the sea.

clue.text: Amazingly solid East German opera heroine

indicators.note: something amazing is wildly out of the ordinary, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A remarkably sturdy East German leading lady of opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' rearranges SOLID plus E; 'East German' looks like one phrase but East supplies the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Tristan und Isolde is a German opera whose title heroine loves Tristan.

clue.text: A turn gone by

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A spin that has already passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, earlier than now, so gone by.

clue.text: Not a full-size horse pistol

definitions.meaning: a young male horse, not yet grown
a revolver made by the American firm founded by Samuel ...

explanation.definitionFit: It is a young male horse, and also a make of revolver.
